content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In mainstream Christian teaching, 'rock' primarily symbolizes God (and, in Christian typology, Christ) as an unshakable foundation, refuge, and source of salvation — connoting stability, permanence, protection, and trustworthiness. The New Testament extends this explicitly to Christ, both as the spiritual rock that accompanied Israel (1 Cor 10:4) and as the sure foundation on which faith and the church are built.", "primary_basis": ["Deuteronomy 32:4 (\"He is the Rock, his works are perfect\")", "Deuteronomy 32:15, 18, 30-31", "Psalm 18:2 (\"The LORD is my rock, my fortress\")", "Psalm 62:2, 6-7", "Psalm 95:1 (\"the rock of our salvation\")", "2 Samuel 22:2-3, 32, 47", "Isaiah 26:4 (\"the LORD... is an everlasting rock\")", "1 Corinthians 10:4 (\"that rock was Christ\", referencing Exodus 17:6 and Numbers 20:8-11)", "Matthew 7:24-25 (the wise man builds his house on the rock)", "1 Peter 2:4-8 and Isaiah 28:16 (Christ as cornerstone/foundation stone)", "Matthew 16:18 (\"on this rock I will build my church\")"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Peter as the rock: in Matthew 16:18, the rock is Peter himself, the foundation of the church and warrant for the papal office (the standard Roman Catholic reading).", "basis": ["Matthew 16:18-19", "John 1:42 (Cephas)"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Peter's confession of faith (or Christ himself) as the rock of Matthew 16:18, rather than Peter's person — the classic Protestant and much patristic reading (e.g., Augustine at times, Chrysostom).", "basis": ["Matthew 16:16-18", "1 Corinthians 3:11", "Ephesians 2:20"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Rock/stone as an object of stumbling and judgment: Christ as a 'stone of stumbling and rock of offense' to unbelievers, and the stone that crushes worldly kingdoms.", "basis": ["Isaiah 8:14", "Romans 9:32-33", "1 Peter 2:7-8", "Psalm 118:22 with Matthew 21:42-44", "Daniel 2:34-35, 44-45"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "The struck rock as a type of Christ's atoning death and the source of living water / the Spirit: the rock struck at Horeb prefiguring Christ smitten so that grace flows out.", "basis": ["Exodus 17:6", "Numbers 20:8-11", "1 Corinthians 10:4", "John 7:37-39", "John 19:34"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Rock as an image of hardness, barrenness, or unresponsiveness (e.g., rocky soil where the seed cannot take root, hearts of stone).", "basis": ["Matthew 13:5-6, 20-21 (parable of the sower)", "Ezekiel 36:26", "Jeremiah 23:29"], "prominence": "minority"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "The core symbolism — God/Christ as rock of refuge, salvation, and foundation — is among the most stable and widely recognized symbols in Christian interpretation, attested from the Hebrew Bible through the New Testament and across patristic, Catholic, Orthodox, and Protestant traditions. The one genuinely contested locus is Matthew 16:18, where the referent of 'this rock' (Peter, Peter's confession, or Christ) divides Catholic and Protestant exegesis; this is a dispute about referent, not about the symbol's basic force (foundation/stability). The 'stumbling stone' and 'struck rock' motifs are complementary rather than competing meanings."}
